structuredContent.summary:
**Finding: exceptional cleanup can still prevent the UNKNOWN report from being saved.** In [run_fixture.py](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/app/examination/windows_platform/run_fixture.py:132), `selector.close()` and the pipe `close()` calls run outside the exception handler. If either raises, `capture_response` exits without returning its prepared limitation, and `main` never writes the report. This leaves the README’s broader claim that exceptional teardown remains reported as unknown unsupported. The new handling does preserve UNKNOWN when `kill()` or the bounded `wait()` fails, provided the subsequent closes succeed. The integration owner should handle close failures without discarding the outcome and add a focused regression.

The reviewed checkout was exactly **`c91621e09d118c001439d65d4425062bb856a913`**, with a clean working tree and required ancestor **`ebf71ce713e4d71a2b32193fd360cfda3cd1dab9`**. I reviewed all six fixture sources; the C# harness and verifier are unchanged from `c5e01df9`. The revised watchdog checks elapsed time after each wake, including a stop wake, before accepting cancellation. Its native termination targets the controller root. These are source observations; the lifecycle has not been exercised.

I independently decompressed the payload in [guarded_bootstrap_attempt.json](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/execution/PKG-01/DEL-01-02/Design/windows_process_fixture_evidence/guarded_bootstrap_attempt.json) and compared it byte-for-byte with the controller Git blob at **`c5e01df9d4a06fa6184841cb30d22ec539e30590`**. All six recorded source hashes and the command hash also match that attempted revision. The attempt returned `prlctl` 255 with “Unable to open new session” and empty stdout. The [outcome](/Users/ryan/.t3/worktrees/chirality-app/t3-0721d905/execution/PKG-01/DEL-01-02/Design/windows_process_fixture_evidence/guarded_bootstrap_outcome.json) correctly records no bootstrap response or new architecture/runtime observation, no native cases, and no requested fixture-owned processes or Jobs. No cleanup or process-exit proof was obtained or needed for a fixture that was not requested.

The remaining substantive gaps are **A: an established namespace guarantee** for the compiler’s actual accesses, and **B: runtime and integration evidence** for the controller and fixture. The sharing-only argument supports refusing the proposed guard; it does not establish universal Windows impossibility. The current source has not reached the guest, and no fixture pass or full repair is established.

This was a read-only static review. I made no guest contact, ran no host or native tests, and made no changes. Acceptance and policy decisions remain with Agent 0; repairs and integration remain with the manager.
